bull_bear.body: Prioritize debt reduction (Roha loan); reinvest Consumer segment profits into A&P; selective EPC project funding; no dividends mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: UP Jal Jeevan Mission fund delays; Roha ramp-up delays in certifications; semiconductor project profitability thresholds; rupee volatility; legacy project execution drag into FY27
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term pain but emphasizes structural improvements, selective bidding, and long-term tailwinds from budget and global trends; confident in Roha’s sustainability edge
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Roha is a zero-liquid discharge plant with circular design — 1/3 CAPEX dedicated to sustainability, making it a global benchmark; this justifies longer payback (4-5 yrs) and is a strategic moat
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt / Equity series shown as (0.6), (0.4), (0.1) and 0.01 against FY23, FY24, FY25 and FY26, with the deck's own comment that the "Ratio within acceptable levels", that "Roha Capex financed by term loan" and that FY25/FY26 had "Lower Operating EBIDTA"; stated intent is to "Continue disciplined Capital Allocation".
- Consolidated non-current borrowings rose ₹1,091 Mn (FY24) → ₹2,521 Mn (FY25) → ₹3,576 Mn (FY26) and current borrowings ₹285 Mn → ₹510 Mn → ₹968 Mn, against total equity of ₹10,198 Mn → ₹12,095 Mn → ₹13,403 Mn.
- Return ratios are shown declining: ROE 24.7%, 23.3%, 21.1%, 18.7%, 11.2% and ROCE 32.5%, 30.0%, 26.9%, 22.0%, 14.3% against FY22 to FY26, with ROE defined as Net Profit/Net worth and ROCE as EBIT/Capital Employed; the deck attributes the fall to "Roha Plant Capex impact", "West Asia crisis impacted gross working capital" and "Reduced Profitability".
- Working Capital Days shown as 91, 99, 94, 91 against FY23 to FY26, with a "High proportion in Treatment Solution segment" and a stated "Focus on improving Working Capital Cycle".
- The deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Engineering: Q3 revenue flat YoY; EBIT down 28% due to UP project delays and international project deferrals; Chemicals: revenue +16% YoY; EBIT down 18% due to Roha depreciation, rupee depreciation, product mix; Consumer: revenue +28% YoY; loss widened to Rs.33M due to heavy A&P investment
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Company snapshot claims "62 + YEARS OF EXPERTISE", operations in 50+ countries, "ONE OF ASIA'S LARGEST SERVICE NETWORKS" and 200,000+ installations world-wide with 3,000+ core industry projects.
- Describes itself as "Leaders in Resins, Membranes & Chemicals, with a Unique End-to-End Portfolio Spanning Solutions, Digital & Services", serving industries, institutions, homes and communities.
- Coverage spans the full water chain — source water and pretreatment, process water, high purity and ultra pure water, industrial wastewater treatment, recycle and Zero Liquid Discharge, drinking water, and municipal and sewage treatment including tertiary recycle and sludge management.
- International revenue share stated at 30%, with global assembly hubs in UAE, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Indonesia and Bangladesh and "EXPORTS ACROSS CONTINENTS".
- Capability set listed as Resins, Membranes, Chemicals, Solutions, Services and Digital.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Segment reporting change] The deck shows a move from Current Reporting (Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products, Lifecycle Services, Specialty Chemicals, Consumer Products) to New Reporting segments: Institutional, Engineering, Chemicals and Consumer Products.
- [Order book] As on 30 June 2026, for Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services: Total Orderbook ~INR 24,730 Mn, of which Engineering projects ~INR 21,820 Mn, Outstanding Sri Lanka ~INR 100 Mn and Outstanding UP SWSM ~INR 2,810 Mn; Bid Pipeline ~INR 97,770 Mn. Engineering projects are stated as excluding the Sri Lanka order, UP SWSM and the recent contract awarded to the company.
- [New contract] A recent contract awarded to the company of USD 52.83 Mn by Hyundai Engineering & Construction is explicitly excluded from the quoted engineering order book.
- [Margin overhang] Recurring structural drags named across slides: "Impact of Higher Cost profile in certain EPC contracts", "Margins continue to be impacted by legacy projects", "Slowed execution of UP Contract", "Impact of West Asia crisis" and "Investment in overseas Geographies".
- [Shareholding, 30 June 2026] Promoter 25.4%, Employee Trust 16.2%, Mutual Funds 12.5%, Foreign Portfolio Investors 4.9%, Alternative Investment Funds 2.8%, Others 38.2%; EPS is stated to include the impact of 2,37,36,140 shares held by IEI/HMIL Shareholding (Staff Welfare) Trusts and 43,78,740 shares held by subsidiaries.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Engineering: margin compression from low-margin UP projects and international mix shift; Chemicals: Roha depreciation (Rs.17M Q3), rupee-driven input cost inflation (pass-through underway); Consumer: negative margin due to strategic A&P spend
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: FY27 to improve on FY26; margin: chemical margin to recover to ~28% long-term; order inflow: expect continued strength in solar/semiconductor/data centers; capex/commissioning: Roha CAPEX complete by Mar’26, full commissioning by FY27, 25% utilization targeted
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.28,330M total; includes Rs.2,050M solar contracts (2 wins), Rs.4,000M UP Jal Jeevan Mission backlog, international EPC projects deferred to Q4FY26
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Semiconductor ultra-pure water & ZLD; green hydrogen; data center water treatment; EU market expansion via acquisition; 200 legacy industrial clusters revival; critical mineral processing
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Engineering margins remain pressured by delayed UP Jal Jeevan Mission execution and international project deferrals, while Roha chemical plant ramp-up is causing EBITDA compression; however, strong order inflows, budget tailwinds in solar/semiconductor/data centers, and long-term margin recovery from Roha create a turning point for FY27.
